title: How Do You Create High-Quality 3D Assets?
author: Legitimate_Crow804
selftext:
Anyone here building web-based games with Three.js or Babylon.js? How do you guys create consistent, high-quality 3D assets?

I've tried using Blender with MCP (without any agent skills), but the results haven't been what I expected.

If you have any tips, tricks, workflows, or hacks for generating better 3D assets, I'd be happy to hear about them.

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: I have Astra create concept art and then comprehensive asset sheets. I use Claude on high to then build the asset in Blender utilizing the asset sheet. After a few iterations I usually have something that I am looking for.

replies.author: Legitimate_Crow804
replies.body: Thank you, but how do you iterating through 100+ assets, sounds like it would be pretty time consuming.

replies.author: PerfectlySplendid
replies.body: Yes. Creating quality is time consuming.

replies.author: Nostradamivre
replies.body: Yes, but it’s way less than creating 100+ assets by hand in a program you don’t know. You have to choose your battles and accept some struggle

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: It is. We arent interested in creating low effort slop. Every single asset in our games is "hand curated" using this method.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
> sounds like it would be pretty time consuming.

Welcome to game development.

comments.author: No-Association-1834
comments.body: Not all AI are good with 3d , Opus5.5 , Astra and Argon are the Top Models that have that Capabilities at pro level , Use lesser or older models and work would be very substandard even with skills and stuff . Muse too have good 3d Gen level and DeepSeek 4.1 is Good .

replies.author: Legitimate_Crow804
replies.body: Hi, I'm using DeepSeek 4.1, and I agree that it's pretty good. I just don't think my current workflow is efficient enough.

replies.author: Haster
replies.body:
How do you avoid deformation when you animate them?

I've used meshy quite a bit but I find it's only good for making static assets; any time I try to do things like attack animations they deform past the point I'm willing to tolerate.

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body:
The only time I have trouble with that is if it's an engine that isn't "supported" but you can still run it through blender and have the AI make sure it doesn't do that. So, this makes it directly import to the engine.

https://i.redd.it/ldel4friwmyh1.png

comments.author: Sbrazen77
comments.body: Anyone that answers without sharing examples should be treated with extreme suspicion. Art is subjective and with the amount of people sharing their self described “gorgeous” ai slop garbage the tips and tricks in this thread should be taken with grain of salt

replies.author: Haster
replies.body: 1000% agreed. It's amazing to me how much people drop their standards because their AI made it for them. The label 'amazing' gets thrown around entirely too easily these days. It's like we're all acting like proud parents about our kids making some markings on a paper.

comments.author: markhobsie
comments.body: I've spent a lot of time trying out Trellis/tripo/meshy/hunyuan etc. And honestly...I've started grabbing as many good free market place assets as I can get my hands on becuase sometimes it's just easier using those, especially now that I can just ask Claude to fix most issues that come with them now.
